message.content:
This is a CBP ruling-type question. A coolant manifold made predominantly of polypropylene, used in a passenger vehicle, could fall under 8708.99 (other parts of motor vehicles) or 3926.90 (other articles of plastics). Since it is a vehicle part, Section XVII Note 2 matters: it excludes parts of general use under Note 2(a), meaning articles of heading 7307, and plastic articles of Chapter 39 are not excluded as parts of general use. A plastic manifold is therefore not excluded from Section XVII. Note 2(b) excludes the parts and accessories listed in Section XVII only for goods in heading 8401-8479 and so on, which does not apply here.

For the Tesla-type thermal management system, the likely 8708 subheading is 8708.99.8180 (other parts and accessories, other). Another option is 8708.99.68, but that is for the other category of non-specified parts. An electric vehicle does not have an engine cooling system in the usual sense, so 8708.91 (radiators) does not fit. 

I recall CBP rulings on Tesla coolant manifolds classifying them in 8708.99.8180. I'll go with that.

{"hts_code": "8708.99.8180", "reason": "The coolant manifold assembly is a dedicated part of a passenger vehicle's thermal management system and is not covered by a more specific 8708 subheading, so it falls in the residual 'other parts and accessories of motor vehicles' provision."}
